2609.21325.title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
2609.21325.paper_summary: Agentic marketplaces are emerging where AI agents with varying capabilities autonomously complete specialized tasks for buyers. A major challenge of such marketplaces is that buyers cannot easily determine which agent will perform best on their tasks. Reported benchmark scores may be difficult to verify or compare across tasks, software, and budgets. We introduce LEGIT, a credentialing protocol connecting certification, reputation, and proposed marketplace allocation. Certification binds measured quality and cost per solved task to an agent configuration, task domain, evaluation budget, and evidence through a signed record. Reputation links records of past task outcomes to the same identity, subject to the reliability of the reported feedback. Buyers and agents can verify credential records and inspect optional visual profiles. Evaluations reveal cost differences between agent configurations with similar observed task success, and show that comparisons depend on the evaluation budget. These results support binding performance measurements to the tested configuration and resource limits. A complementary analysis quantifies the deposits and fees required for reputation manipulation under a stated Sybil attack model.
2609.21325.paper_summary_zh: 代理市場正在出現，AI代理擁有不同的能力，自主地為買家完成專門任務。這類市場的一個主要挑戰是，買家無法輕易確定哪個代理在他們的任務中表現最佳。報告的基準分數可能難以驗證或在任務、軟體和預算之間進行比較。我們介紹了LEGIT，一種將認證、聲譽和提議的市場分配連接起來的認證協議。認證將測量的質量和每個解決任務的成本與代理配置、任務領域、評估預算和通過簽名記錄的證據綁定在一起。聲譽將過去任務結果的記錄鏈接到相同的身份，這取決於報告反饋的可靠性。買家和代理可以驗證認證記錄並檢查可選的視覺檔案。評估揭示了在觀察到的任務成功相似的代理配置之間的成本差異，並顯示比較依賴於評估預算。這些結果支持將性能測量綁定到測試的配置和資源限制上。一項補充分析量化了在所述的Sybil攻擊模型下，聲譽操縱所需的存款和費用。
